summary:
Supernovel introduces Rhizobove, the name is a play on words, combining "Rhizosphere" + "Above", which is an advanced decision-support framework that bridges macro-scale space telemetry with micro-scale soil biology to protect agricultural rhizosphere health in extreme arid environments like the Al-Ahsa Oasis.

• What was developed: A predictive intelligence platform framework that ingests NASA Earth observation data-specifically NASA POWER root-zone soil wetness (0-100 cm), ECOSTRESS/POWER land skin temperature, and NDVI vegetation indices-to monitor invisible abiotic stress in date palm root zones.

• How it addresses the challenge: While satellites cannot see underground, Rhizobove translates orbital data into biological tipping points. When root-zone moisture drops below optimal levels (<0.25) and thermal spikes exceed 35-40 C (which denatures vital nitrogen-fixing enzymes), the system triggers automated alerts for targeted bio-inoculant application.

• Why it is important: By shifting agriculture from a reactive response to proactive, space-guided microbiome protection, Rhizobove prevents root-zone collapse, preserves vital nitrogen fixation, and secures food and crop resilience against climate extremes.
details:
*What does it do, how does it work?
Farmers usually treat damage once it has shown on the surface, such as leaf wilting, when it could be tackled and even prevented much earlier. That's where Rhizobove comes in, it will bridge the gap by linking NASA's extensive data, from recorded vital numbers and satellite imagery, to biology and agriculture. Enhancing soil and crops with micro-organisms and the possibility of using/producing GMOs to handle arid environments, while monitoring data feedback from an application/website.


*Intended Impact
Food Security & Climate Resilience: Protects Saudi Arabia’s core agricultural yield-starting with Al-Ahsa’s 2.5+ million date palm against escalating climate extremes, thermal spikes, and soil salinity.
Microbial Conservation: Preserves native and inoculated soil biodiversity in harsh desert environments where traditional farming inputs frequently fail due to extreme heat.

*Tools
The project is delivered as a robust systems architecture and scientific data model, defining the exact data pipelines, threshold logic, and interface blueprints required for full technical deployment. NASA POWER (Data Access Viewer) was used to gather data regarding parameters affecting soil health, such was root zone soil wetness, earth skin temperature, evapotranspiration.

*Creativity
Linking orbital satellite telemetry with microscopic soil biology to shift management from reactive to preventive

*Considerations
Addressing the harsh realities of extreme arid environments, ensuring scientific rigor, and navigating the technical challenges of application building and harmonizing coarse-resolution NASA satellite grids (~9 km spatial resolution) with localized oasis-level farm management.
